title: Backups that nobody tested are a hope, not a plan
body: Postmortems across decades rhyme: GitLab found five backup layers failing at once; countless smaller firms find theirs only during the fire. A restore test converts an assumption into evidence, and scheduling it converts evidence into a habit. The industry's most repeated incident sentence might be 'we thought we had backups'. If a fact can save one database, it is this one.
source_hint: Cross-industry postmortem pattern; GitLab 2017 as exemplar
